newsitem.title: GERMANY: AGAB bank owners offer to buy out shareholders.
newsitem.headline: AGAB bank owners offer to buy out shareholders.

text.p: The two banks owning major stakes in AGAB AG, DG Bank and the Landwirtschafliche Rentenbank, have offered to buy out AGAB shareholders at 125 marks a share, AGAB said in a statement.
AGAB said the reason for the proposed buy out was that it expected to lose 175 million marks this year. The company also said it would not pay a dividend in the medium term.

AGAB said the primary reason for losses was competition from the Roth group as well as continuing balance precautionary measures.
AGAB said the buy-out offer was expected to last until December 23, when an application will be made for the discontinuation of the bourse listing.
"The concept of AGAB as a listed company has not proved viable," AGAB said in a statement.
The action of the large shareholders was supported by the executive committee of AGAB, it said, adding that the move had no consequences for the commitments of the company.
Rather, AGAB said, the aim of the buy-out was to continue to work with partners in development concepts and to translate them into trusting work together.
